directions.challenged_assumption: Failure should be interpreted through a particular added state or named mechanism rather than through transformation laws directly testable in the observations.
competing_explanations: The residual response is equivariant under the same translations, reflections, and rotations as the resolved dynamics.
The residual contains a reproducible symmetry-selective component associated with orientation or position.
Apparent symmetry breaking is introduced by boundaries or discretization.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Create symmetry-related copies of each localized perturbation at boundary-matched positions, run them from correspondingly transformed initial conditions, and repeat after halving the grid spacing.
measurements: Equivariance error between each response and the transformed reference response
Change in those quantities under grid refinement and increased boundary separation

opposing_predictions.prediction: Transformed residual fields coincide within the deterministic numerical floor, and held-out responses are predicted by transforming a reference response.
One or more residual components remain tied to absolute orientation or position, reproduce across initial conditions, and predict the favored response in held-out perturbations.
The apparent violation decreases at the discretization convergence rate or with greater boundary separation.

evidence_dependency: fixed-template-recovery showed that representation-aligned recovery can manufacture apparent conceptual success.
closure-and-skill-route showed that predictive closure detects failure without identifying its organizing cause.
directions.local_feasibility: A small deterministic two-dimensional simulator needs only a few transformed runs per perturbation; field transformations and norm comparisons are CPU-cheap.
directions.negative_result_value: An equivariant result would eliminate symmetry selection and establish that subsequent hypotheses should respect the measured transformation law.
directions.novelty_risk: Moderate: symmetry tests are established; value would require a residual symmetry signature that predicts interventions rather than merely redescribing the equations.
directions.research_question: Do failed predictions reveal a reproducible symmetry-selective response that is absent from the resolved dynamics?
directions.stop_criterion: Kill the symmetry-selective direction if violations never exceed five times the refinement-estimated numerical floor on held-out initial conditions, or if every violation vanishes at the numerical convergence rate or with boundary separation.
directions.why_nontrivial: The experiment tests an observable law across interventions and coordinate copies; it neither searches for a planted equation nor treats improved fitting as mechanistic evidence.

directions.challenged_assumption: All scientifically relevant influence in the failed model can be represented by a finite-range local closure.
competing_explanations: Perturbation influence has a finite propagation cone and rapidly decaying spatial kernel.
The response contains a reproducible long-range component whose scale grows with the domain.
Long-range effects are boundary reflections or global normalization artifacts.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Apply equal-integral compact perturbations of several widths at multiple boundary-matched locations, then repeat on two domain sizes while preserving local resolution and dimensionless conditions.
measurements: Response amplitude versus distance before any boundary return
Collapse of distance-response curves in local coordinates versus domain-normalized coordinates
Dependence on perturbation width at fixed integral

opposing_predictions.prediction: Arrival times define a stable finite-speed cone, and pre-arrival distant responses remain at the numerical floor on both domain sizes.
Responses occur outside every cone supported by near-field arrivals and follow a distance law that reproduces on held-out source locations and domain sizes.
The distant component shifts with boundary-return time or collapses only after normalization by total domain size.

evidence_dependency: llm-memory-hypothesis underperformed state-free alternatives, motivating a direct response-law question without presuming extra state.
closure-and-skill-route established unexplained predictive structure but could not identify its cause.
directions.local_feasibility: Impulse-response maps on modest grids can be accumulated deterministically in minutes, with two small domain sizes sufficient for the initial discrimination.
directions.negative_result_value: Absence of out-of-cone response would bound the admissible interaction range and focus later work on local explanations; domain dependence would identify an artifact control that future tests must include.
directions.novelty_risk: Moderate to high: locality diagnostics are familiar, so novelty would depend on discovering a stable, intervention-predictive distance law not implied by the baseline.
directions.research_question: Does the unexplained response obey a finite propagation law, or is there an intervention-reproducible influence outside every locally inferred propagation cone?
directions.stop_criterion: Kill the intrinsic long-range direction if all pre-arrival distant responses stay below five times the numerical floor across held-out locations, or if apparent distant responses track boundary-return time or domain-wide normalization.
directions.why_nontrivial: Domain scaling and arrival-time ordering distinguish physical spatial organization from a flexible residual fit and from boundary contamination.

directions.challenged_assumption: Failures produced by multiple perturbations can be understood as the sum of failures produced by each perturbation separately.
competing_explanations: Residual responses compose additively after accounting for the resolved model.
Two perturbations generate an irreducible interaction with a characteristic separation or timing dependence.
The apparent interaction is ordinary instantaneous amplitude saturation rather than a distinct cooperative response.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Use a preregistered factorial design containing perturbation A alone, B alone, A and B together, and amplitude-matched single controls; sweep A-B distance, pulse order, and pulse lag, then reserve several combinations as held-out tests.
measurements: Interaction contrast R(A+B)-R(A)-R(B)+R(0) in prediction space
Interaction magnitude versus distance and pulse lag
Order asymmetry between A-then-B and B-then-A
Performance on held-out factorial combinations without refitting

opposing_predictions.prediction: The interaction contrast remains at the deterministic floor for every distance, lag, and held-out combination.
A nonzero contrast has a reproducible distance-lag profile and correctly predicts held-out joint responses from the preregistered factorial law.
The contrast is reproduced by amplitude-matched single controls, depends on simultaneous total amplitude, and has no additional pulse-order signature.

evidence_dependency: llm-memory-hypothesis showed that an appealing named mechanism can lose to state-free alternatives under intervention.
null-world-control showed that fitting can set an unnecessary effect to zero, suggesting that a decisive proposal should include an exact null contrast.
fixed-template-recovery showed why success must be defined by held-out response structure rather than recovery of planted form.
directions.local_feasibility: The factorial contrasts require only a small grid of deterministic simulations and simple array arithmetic, readily completing within 30 minutes on one CPU.
directions.negative_result_value: A null contrast would establish an additive regime and provide a stringent certificate against cooperative stories; saturation-only behavior would redirect attention to the resolved instantaneous response.
directions.novelty_risk: Moderate: factorial interaction tests are standard, and scientific novelty would require a stable distance-lag law with new predictive consequences.
directions.research_question: Do failed predictions contain an irreducible cooperative response to paired perturbations, with a measurable spatial or temporal interaction scale?
directions.stop_criterion: Kill the cooperative-response direction if interaction contrasts remain below five times the numerical floor on all held-out combinations, or if amplitude-matched instantaneous saturation predicts them within that tolerance.
directions.why_nontrivial: The factorial null is algebraically sharp, while distance, lag, order, and amplitude controls separate cooperation from additivity and generic nonlinearity.

directions.challenged_assumption: The observed failure is a roughly uniform misspecification rather than evidence concentrated near a qualitative transition.
competing_explanations: Residual error changes smoothly with intervention amplitude and reflects distributed misspecification.
A transition boundary organizes the failure, producing branch changes and divergent recovery or susceptibility.
A sharp boundary is a timestep, grid, or finite-duration artifact.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Sweep a scalar perturbation amplitude adaptively through the region where held-out error rises, approach each amplitude from both directions and several initial conditions, and repeat the sweep with halved timestep, refined grid, and doubled observation duration.
measurements: Long-time outcome class and branch occupancy
Recovery time and finite-difference susceptibility versus amplitude
Location and width of any transition under numerical refinement and longer observation

opposing_predictions.prediction: Outcomes, recovery times, and susceptibilities vary continuously, with no refinement-stable branch boundary or growing timescale.
A stable critical region exhibits a branch change, sharply increasing recovery time or susceptibility, and reproducible initial-condition dependence that predicts held-out amplitudes.
The apparent boundary moves materially or disappears when timestep, grid, or observation duration changes.

evidence_dependency: closure-and-skill-route found predictive nonclosure but no cause, leaving open whether failure is localized around a regime boundary.
llm-memory-hypothesis failed its discriminating intervention, indicating that a qualitatively different intervention geometry should be tested.
directions.local_feasibility: A coarse adaptive one-parameter sweep followed by refinement near any sharp change limits the number of CPU simulations and fits the 30-minute initial budget.
directions.negative_result_value: A converged smooth response would rule out transition-centered explanations and justify treating the residual as distributed; numerical drift would expose a simulator artifact.
directions.novelty_risk: Moderate: bifurcation diagnostics are mature, so novelty depends on a previously unrecognized transition law that explains and predicts the recorded intervention failures.
directions.research_question: Is the predictive failure concentrated around a genuine dynamical transition rather than caused by uniform model inadequacy?
directions.stop_criterion: Kill the transition direction if convergence-refined response curves remain smooth with bounded recovery time and susceptibility, show no stable branch change, and predict held-out amplitudes without a transition term.
directions.why_nontrivial: The question concerns qualitative organization of observable dynamics, and numerical-refinement controls prevent a sharp plotting feature from being mistaken for a scientific transition.

directions.challenged_assumption: A scientifically grounded hypothesis should depend on evidence relations, yet the fixed-template and workflow results leave open whether proposals instead depend on superficial representation.
competing_explanations: Hypothesis content and proposed discriminating interventions are stable under invertible evidence-preserving reparameterizations.
Proposal content changes with notation, units, ordering, or coordinate choice despite unchanged evidence.
Only verbal labels vary while operational predictions remain invariant.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Generate blinded packets related by preregistered invertible transformations: unit changes, variable permutations, coordinate rotations, time rescaling with all derived quantities transformed, and reordered summaries. Run isolated calls with identical instructions, then automatically translate every quantitative prediction back to a canonical coordinate system and execute the proposed interventions locally.
measurements: Agreement of canonicalized directional and quantitative predictions
Held-out prediction scores for each transformed packet
Within-transformation variability compared with variability across genuinely different evidence packets

opposing_predictions.prediction: Canonicalized interventions and opposing predictions agree across transformations, and their held-out outcomes are statistically indistinguishable.
Evidence-equivalent packets yield incompatible canonical interventions or opposing predictions, with disagreement exceeding repeated-call variability.
Mechanism names differ, but canonical interventions, signs, thresholds, and held-out outcomes agree.

evidence_dependency: fixed-template-recovery demonstrated success when benchmark truth and representation were aligned.
closure-and-skill-route found that a workflow skill added formatting but no scientific content.
llm-memory-hypothesis showed that one packet elicited both memory and state-free stories, raising a representation-sensitivity question.
directions.local_feasibility: Packet transformations, isolated calls, canonicalization, and a small number of deterministic intervention runs require no training, labels, web access, or GPU computation.
directions.negative_result_value: Instability would provide a falsifiable limit on claims of autonomous concept formation and identify which representation changes must become mandatory controls; invariance would justify evaluating proposals primarily through operational predictions.
directions.novelty_risk: High: robustness to reparameterization is broadly studied. A contribution would require linking transformation instability specifically to executable scientific predictions, not merely comparing generated wording.
directions.research_question: Are executable research hypotheses derived from failed experiments invariant under evidence-preserving reparameterizations?
directions.stop_criterion: Kill the invariance direction if canonicalized intervention choices or opposing predictions disagree across equivalent packets more than across repeated calls to the same packet, even when lexical labels are ignored.
directions.why_nontrivial: This is an empirical question about scientific inference behavior, not a software architecture proposal; executing canonicalized predictions distinguishes semantic invariance from superficial textual similarity.

selection_reason: Selected ex ante because the paired-perturbation factorial contrast supplies the sharpest local null, distinguishes three live explanations with held-out interventions, avoids assuming a hidden variable, and yields useful bounds even when the cooperative hypothesis is killed.
